content:
Here is the translation of this passage from Homer's Iliad (Book 19, lines 184-197):

Then the lord of men Agamemnon spoke to him again:
"I rejoice, son of Laertes, hearing your speech;
for you have gone through everything fittingly and set it forth in order.
These things I am willing to swear, and my heart urges me to do so,
nor will I swear falsely before the god. But let Achilles
wait here meanwhile, eager though he is for battle;
and let all you others wait assembled, until the gifts
come from my tent and we make our faithful oaths.
And to you yourself I give this charge and command:
having chosen the best young men of all the Achaeans,
bring from my ship the gifts which yesterday
we promised to give to Achilles, and bring the women too.
And let Talthybius quickly throughout the wide army of the Achaeans
prepare a boar for me to sacrifice to Zeus and to Helios."

[This passage shows Agamemnon responding to Odysseus (the son of Laertes), agreeing to make formal oaths of reconciliation with Achilles, and organizing the delivery of the promised gifts and the preparation of a sacrifice to seal the oath.]
